content:
GOAL: pick one coupling position that uses the round-1 measured behaviour-graph curvature WITHOUT spending codebook radius, and check it against the four failure modes already recorded (CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ radius spending -> 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, recall 0.0419; BRad-RQ radial placement; CURVCTRL-SID level learning rate; poincare-frechet codebook updates).
READ: the round brief for round_20261102_071156_961, plus the outcome summaries of rounds 20261028_233100_128, 20261029_030015_260, 20261029_093253_576 and the round_20261102_031529_470 post-mortem (kappa_hat [0.00,-8.96,-25.55] -> delta [0.702,0.298,-1.000] -> radius [0.0381,0.0312,0.0163]; frozen baseline 247/7414/20223 SIDs, recall 0.055537; target 0.065).
OBSERVED/REASONED: (i) a level-uniform curvature shift multiplied into every codeword's distance cancels in the argmin, so any per-level c_l spent on the metric can only change posterior sharpness, never the partition - therefore the only way curvature can move SIDs without touching a radius is a code-LOCAL field; (ii) the round-1 collapse came from rho_l entering the codeword scale, so the safe invariant is: codeword parameterisation, update rule, count and radius byte-identical to baseline, curvature enters only inside the assignment score; (iii) the Poincare distance from the origin reduces to 2*artanh(sqrt(c)*||u||), so a per-code curvature becomes a single scalar gain inside an artanh - cheap, exact, and boundable.
DECISION: propose CURVCHART-RESGUARD: per-codeword Poincare chart curvature derived from the null-standardised training-graph Ollivier curvature of the items each code covered last epoch, applied only as a bounded gain inside the RQ assignment distance, with a [0.5,2]x volume guard on each code's accepting radius. Resolution protection is structural (radius/count/update untouched), not empirical.
STILL OPEN: whether a bounded 2x metric perturbation is large enough to move prefix predictability, and whether Stage 3 can exploit a rebalanced partition; both are one-run observations, not gates.

ANSWER RECORD (idea 1 of 1, full text emitted in the reply):
IDEA CURVCHART-RESGUARD - per-codeword Poincare chart curvature from the null-standardised training transition-graph Ollivier curvature, spent only as a gain g_e = exp(-s_e/2) inside the RQ-VAE assignment distance q_e = artanh(clip(tanh(1)*g_e*||r-e||/rho_l)), with the codeword parameters, codebook radius, code count and codebook update rule held byte-identical to the inherited baseline, and a hard [0.5,2]x guard band on every code's accepting radius relative to the neutral chart. Switches: BEHAVIOUR_OFF sets s_e = 0 (all gains 1, partition provably equals the Euclidean argmin because artanh(tanh(1)*x) is a common strictly increasing map); GEOMETRY_OFF replaces q_e by the Euclidean ratio ||r-e||/rho_l with s_e still computed but unused; BOTH_ON is the full field. Curvature is gradient-free (precomputed item-graph tensor, no_grad), standardised against an R=8 size-preserving member-shuffle null, clipped to +-3. Cross-rank statistics use all_reduce (never a rank-0 broadcast); the graph curvature is computed redundantly per rank or read from an identical per-rank file. Cost: <2% wall clock per step (3 levels x B x 256 artanh, ~0.2 ms/step on GPU), one-time CPU curvature pass over the 24556-item training graph. No ablation arm is trained.
